intro: Cashiers build service orientation, people-reading and coordination skills that banks, offices and post offices hire for. Of the 25 careers below, Tellers match cashiers best at 93%, and 24 of the 25 pay more than the $32,880 cashier median.
why_it_works: Running a register means handling money accurately, keeping a line moving and staying friendly with every customer. O*NET rates service orientation at 3.12 out of 5 for cashiers, which is why teller, customer service and front desk roles rank so high. Most of these jobs use the same cash, counting and conversation skills with steadier schedules. Tellers do much of the same work in a bank. The gaps include problem solving and quality control.
tips: Start with banks and credit unions, since tellers are the closest match and usually train you on the job.
Mention your cash accuracy on your resume, such as drawers balanced or errors caught.
Apply for a shift lead or front-end supervisor role to build the problem-solving skills higher-paying matches ask for.

faq.q: What jobs can former cashiers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Tellers (93%), Customer Service Representatives (90%), Gambling Cage Workers (89%) and Postal Service Clerks (89%), based on O*NET 31.0. Pharmacy Aides (86%) and Hotel, Motel, and Resort Desk Clerks (86%) are also good fits.

faq.q: Which jobs pay more than being a cashier?
faq.a: 24 of the 25 matches pay more than the $32,880 cashier median in BLS May 2025 data. Postal Service Clerks earn $62,130 (+89%), Credit Authorizers, Checkers, and Clerks earn $50,080 (+52%) and First-Line Supervisors of Retail Sales Workers earn $48,520 (+48%).

faq.q: Can a cashier get a better job without a degree?
faq.a: Yes. 24 of the 25 matches usually need no more education than a cashier job, based on O*NET Job Zones. Tellers, the closest match, usually train on the job for up to 1 month, and 73% of tellers have a high school diploma or the equivalent.

faq.q: What jobs are similar to being a cashier?
faq.a: In sales and customer-facing work, the nearest roles are Counter and Rental Clerks (89% match), Retail Salespersons (88%) and Gambling Change Persons and Booth Cashiers (84%). These keep the same customer skills while changing what you sell or handle.
